articles.title: India Amends Textile PLI Scheme: New Investment Criteria & Round 4 Incentives - India Briefing
articles.summary: India Amends Textile PLI Scheme: New Investment Criteria & Round 4 Incentives  India Briefing
articles.full_text:
The central government has announced amendments to India’s Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles in a notification issued on 28 October 2026. Through the 2026 amendments, the Union Ministry of Textiles aims to address implementation-related challenges and provide greater flexibility to businesses seeking incentives for investments in man-made fibre (MMF) textiles and technical textiles.
It primarily introduces revised investment and turnover thresholds, differentiated incentive structures under two scheme categories, provisions allowing existing participants to migrate to the fourth application round (Round 4), and an extended implementation timeline. Round 4 of the registration and application window is now open on the official website between 1 November and 31 December 2026.
It should be noted that the detailed operational guidelines incorporating the 2026 amendments will be issued separately. These guidelines are expected to provide further clarity on the implementation of the revised provisions.
Establish Manufacturing Operations
We support foreign manufacturers with market assessment, site selection, PLI incentives, and investment structuring.
India PLI Scheme for textile: Revised investment and turnover threshold in Round 4
India’s 2026 amendment for textile PLI establishes two categories under the scheme, with different minimum investment and turnover requirements. Both thresholds must be met for a company to qualify for incentives.
Scheme Part I
Under Part I, eligible applicants must meet the following criteria:
- Invest at least INR 1.5 billion in plant and machinery, equipment, and civil works
- Exclude land and administrative building costs when calculating eligible investment
- Achieve a minimum turnover of INR 6 billion through the manufacture and sale of products covered under the notified MMF and technical textile categories
The incentive structure is as follows:
- Performance Year 1: Companies receive an incentive of 15 per cent on turnover, subject to achieving the prescribed minimum turnover
- Performance Years 2-5: PLI applicants/companies must achieve at least 10 per cent incremental turnover compared to the previous year’s turnover
- Declining incentive rate: The incentive rate decreases by one percentage point annually, starting at 14 per cent in Year 2 and reaching 11 per cent in Year 5
Scheme Part II
Part II provides a lower investment and turnover threshold, making the scheme accessible to applicants with comparatively smaller investment plans.
Eligible applicants must meet the following criteria:
- Invest at least INR 500 million in plant and machinery, equipment, and civil works
- Exclude land and administrative building costs from eligible investment
- Achieve a minimum turnover of INR 1 billion through the manufacture and sale of notified MMF and technical textile products
The incentive structure is as follows:
- Performance Year 1: Companies receive an incentive of 11 per cent on turnover, subject to achieving the prescribed minimum turnover
- Performance Years 2-5: PLI applicants/companies must achieve at least 10 per cent incremental turnover over compared to the previous year’s turnover
- Declining incentive rate: The incentive rate decreases by one percentage point annually, starting at 10 per cent in Year 2 and reaching 7 per cent in Year 5
Common condition
Under both categories, only sales transacted through normal banking channels will qualify for calculating eligible turnover and incentives.
Migration of existing textile PLI participants to Round 4
Amendments to the textile PLI scheme allow existing participating companies from Rounds 1, 2 and 3 to migrate to Round 4, subject to specific conditions.
Companies that have not claimed or received any incentives under their existing applications can opt for Round 4. However, they must withdraw their existing applications under the earlier rounds, as applicable, to become eligible for migration.
This provision gives existing participants an opportunity to participate under the revised investment and incentive framework rather than continue under their earlier application conditions.
Treatment of investments already made by migrating applicants
Recent changes also clarify how investments made before Round 4 will be considered when calculating eligible investment for companies migrating from earlier rounds.
The following provisions apply:
- Eligible investment period: Investments made between 24 September 2021 (the date the PLI Scheme was introduced) and 31 March 2026 will be considered at their actual cost.
- Condition for investment recognition: This treatment applies where the applicant has not commenced production or generated turnover from the investment.
- Depreciation adjustment: If production or turnover has already commenced, depreciation on the capitalised assets will be charged for the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
- Depreciation calculation: The depreciation rate will be determined in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013.
These provisions are specifically intended for applicants migrating from earlier rounds. They do not apply to new applicants applying directly under Round 4.
Extension of the textile PLI scheme implementation period
The amendment extends the PLI Scheme’s implementation timeline for Round 4 participants until FY 2033-34. FY 2032-33 will be the final performance year, while FY 2033-34 will be the final year for claiming incentives.
The revised implementation schedule provides two years of gestation before the commencement of the five performance years.
| Scheme period | Financial year | 
| Gestation Year 1 | FY 2026-27 | 
| Gestation Year 2 | FY 2027-28 | 
| Performance Year 1 | FY 2028-29 | 
| Performance Year 2 | FY 2029-30 | 
| Performance Year 3 | FY 2030-31 | 
| Performance Year 4 | FY 2031-32 | 
| Performance Year 5 | FY 2032-33 | 
| Final incentive claim year | FY 2033-34 | 
The corresponding incentive claims will be made in the financial year immediately following each performance year. For instance, incentives for FY 2028-29 will be claimed in FY 2029-30.
Evaluate PLI Incentives
Assess your eligibility for the Textile PLI Scheme, understand the revised investment and turnover criteria, and identify available incentives.
What the PLI scheme amendments mean for textile manufacturers and investors
Indi’s revised framework has several implications for businesses considering investments in India’s MMF and technical textile segments.
- Greater flexibility in investment planning: The introduction of two investment categories, with thresholds of INR 1.5 billion and INR 500 million, provides different entry points for businesses with varying investment capacities.
- Performance-linked incentive structure: Companies must meet both the minimum investment and turnover requirements. They must also demonstrate at least 10 per cent incremental turnover growth annually from Performance Year 2 onwards to qualify for subsequent incentives.
- Migration opportunities for existing participants: Companies that have not claimed or received incentives under earlier rounds can consider migrating to Round 4, subject to withdrawing their existing applications.
- Recognition of historical investments: Eligible investments made between 24 September 2021 and 31 March 2026 can be considered at actual cost for migrating applicants, subject to the conditions governing commencement of production or turnover and depreciation.
- Longer implementation and investment horizon: The two-year gestation period, followed by five performance years, gives participating businesses additional time to establish production capacity. It can also help companies achieve the prescribed turnover thresholds.
India PLI Scheme for textile: Progress & performance as of March 2026
As of 31 March 2026, the central government has approved 170 companies under the PLI scheme for textiles.

| Technical textiles | 89 | 278.32 billion | 1.69 trillion | 120,205 | 
| Total | 170 | 415.33 billion | 2.75 trillion | 367,427 | 
Source: PLI, Ministry of Textile, Government of India
These companies had collectively recorded actual investments of approximately INR 81.17 billion and generated 33,427 jobs across various states and union territories.

articles.title: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports: Report - The Times of India
articles.summary: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports: Report  The Times of India
articles.full_text:
The government has moved to resolve a dispute over Scotch whisky imports under the UK trade pact, assuring liquor companies that bulk shipments qualify for the reduced 75 percent import duty after tax officials questioned their eligibility for the concession.
According to a Reuters report citing six people with direct knowledge of the matter, commerce ministry officials gave the assurance during a closed-door meeting with liquor industry executives on Monday, saying New Delhi would honour the trade agreement in letter and spirit.
One government source said, "We are potentially moving towards a resolution. Bulk Scotch whisky imports are indeed part of concessions under the trade deal."
A second source said commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told attendees that necessary steps were being taken to address the issue "so that the duty concession on bulk Scotch whisky is not impaired".
The dispute centres on the agreement to reduce import duty on Scotch whisky in India from 150 per cent to 75 percent under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which came into effect in July 2026. 
However, tax officials had told liquor companies that the reduced duty did not apply to Scotch imported in bulk containers.
The disagreement is significant because around 80 percent of Scotch whisky shipped to India arrives in bulk rather than in finished bottles.
These imports are used by Indian manufacturers to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky by blending Scotch with other spirits and ingredients. The industry maintains that both bottled and bulk Scotch imports should qualify for the reduced tariff under the trade agreement.
The dispute has affected major liquor companies, including Diageo and Pernod Ricard, as well as Indian manufacturers Radico Khaitan and Allied Blenders and Distillers. Tax officials searched the offices of several companies in recent days and questioned executives over the classification and eligibility of bulk Scotch imports.
The issue has also drawn attention from Britain and Scotland. The British government said it was working with New Delhi to resolve the matter, while the Scottish government separately raised concerns over the treatment of bulk Scotch imports.
Scotch exports to India were valued at $335 million in 2024, and the Scotch Whisky Association has projected that the trade agreement could increase exports by an additional $1.34 billion over five years.
